skill.name: brenda-database
skill.description: Explore BRENDA enzyme records through documented SOAP workflows for kinetic parameters, reactions, organisms, environmental conditions, visualization, and pathway analysis.
skill.summary: Analyze BRENDA enzyme kinetics, organism evidence, and pathway options.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Review confirmed three medium-severity arbitrary file overwrite paths and one medium-severity import-hijacking risk. The other 182 static findings are false positives from EC numbers, Markdown formatting, ordinary imports, credential setup documentation, and official URLs. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, obfuscated execution, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Caller-supplied export and report paths can truncate existing files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict outputs to a dedicated directory, reject traversal, and require explicit confirmation before replacing an existing file.

remediation.issue: A broad ancestor directory is appended before importing `brenda_client`.
remediation.suggestion: Package `brenda_client` with relative imports and remove the `sys.path` mutation. Pin and verify any external dependency.

remediation.issue: The main query module contains invalid Python syntax at line 559.
remediation.suggestion: Correct the conditional expression and run compilation tests for every included Python module before publication.

remediation.issue: The documented `brenda_client` module is not included in the skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Include the client module or declare a verified package dependency with an exact version.

content.user_title: Query and Analyze BRENDA Enzyme Data
content.value_statement: Comparing enzyme evidence across organisms and substrates requires repetitive BRENDA searches and manual parsing. This skill organizes authenticated queries, comparisons, visualizations, exports, and pathway analysis.
actual_capabilities: Parses BRENDA Km and reaction response strings into structured enzyme, organism, substrate, condition, and literature fields.
Defines searches and comparisons for substrates, products, organisms, pH, temperature, cofactors, inhibitors, and activators.
Provides plots for kinetic distributions, organism comparisons, pH profiles, temperature profiles, substrate specificity, and Michaelis-Menten curves.
Builds retrosynthetic pathway structures and estimates enzyme availability, feasibility, operating conditions, and substitution options.
Exports kinetic tables, pathway reports, and visualizations in common research formats.
Documents BRENDA SOAP endpoints, authentication parameters, response formats, errors, and query examples.
limitations: The included query module has invalid syntax at line 559 and cannot import until corrected.
The required `brenda_client` module is referenced but not included in this skill package.
Live queries require a BRENDA account, credentials, network access, and third-party Python dependencies.
Pathway scores are heuristic, and literature records may have missing units, inconsistent conditions, or limited organism coverage.

use_cases.title: Compare Enzyme Kinetics
use_cases.description: Compare Km evidence for one EC number across organisms, substrates, temperatures, and pH conditions.

use_cases.title: Screen Engineering Candidates
use_cases.description: Identify thermostable, pH-stable, cofactor-compatible, or inhibitor-tolerant enzyme candidates for experimental review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Summaries
use_cases.description: Transform BRENDA records into comparison tables, plots, and cited summaries for downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find Enzyme Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one enzyme and substrate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Km values for EC {{ec_number}} and substrate {{substrate}}. Summarize organisms, units, conditions, and literature notes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Organisms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare EC {{ec_number}} across {{organisms}}. Rank evidence by Km, temperature, pH, substrate, and number of available records.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Engineering Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen EC {{ec_number}} for {{target_condition}}. Compare stability, cofactors, inhibitors, activators, kinetic evidence, and data gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Candidate Pathway
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pathway analysis with evidence review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a candidate enzymatic pathway from {{starting_materials}} to {{target_product}} within {{max_steps}} steps. Report enzymes, organisms, conditions, cofactors, feasibility, and uncertainties.

output_examples.input: Compare alcohol dehydrogenase evidence across yeast, E. coli, and humans.
output_examples.output: A comparison table lists each organism, substrate, Km range, conditions, and record count. Missing units and sparse records are clearly marked.

output_examples.input: Visualize the available kinetic evidence for one EC number.
output: A kinetic distribution chart grouped by organism and substrate.
A condition summary covering pH and temperature evidence.
A short note explaining missing values and comparison limits.

output_examples.input: Assess a three-step pathway to lactate.
output_examples.output: A pathway summary identifies candidate enzymes, organisms, cofactors, operating conditions, feasibility factors, and experimental validation needs.

best_practices: Verify EC numbers, substrate names, units, assay conditions, and literature notes before comparing records.
Keep BRENDA credentials outside prompts and version control, and limit file permissions for local environment files.
Treat pathway rankings as hypotheses and confirm candidates with primary literature and laboratory validation.
anti_patterns: Do not place account passwords in prompts, source files, exported reports, or committed environment files.
Do not pass unreviewed absolute paths or existing filenames to export and report functions.
Do not rank enzymes by Km alone without aligning substrates, units, temperatures, pH values, and assay methods.

faq.question: Does this skill require a BRENDA account?
faq.answer: Yes. Live SOAP queries require an active BRENDA account and valid email and password credentials.

faq.question: Are credentials included with the skill?
faq.answer: No. Users must provide their own credentials and protect them from prompts, logs, and version control.

faq.question: Can the included scripts run immediately?
faq.answer: No. The query module has a syntax error, and the referenced `brenda_client` module is absent.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The source defines CSV, JSON, Excel, text report, and image outputs, subject to available dependencies.

faq.question: Can results support enzyme engineering decisions?
faq.answer: They can support screening, but users must verify literature context, units, assay conditions, and experimental feasibility.

faq.question: Does pathway analysis prove a route will work?
faq.answer: No. Pathway feasibility is heuristic and requires biochemical review, thermodynamic analysis, and experimental validation.
